title: An impurity of a module above a point descends along a directed limit of affine schemes
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that an impurity of a module above a point, presented over a directed limit of affine schemes, already appears at some finite stage of the system (statement lines 4572-4580, tag 05IZ). The proof reduces to a single emptiness assertion after observing that the associated point condition transports by base change, and then gives two genuinely different arguments: the first writes the (empty) fibre product of the closure with the residue field as a filtered limit of quasi-compact pieces so that one piece must be empty, and the second separates the closed set from the special fibre by a locally finitely presented replacement morphism and descends that replacement, together with an affine open neighbourhood, to a stage of the system. The descent of the replacement morphism is the substance, so the claim is H2.
